messages:
Maya: Heads-up — starting Lucid22B onboarding. initial hosted runs look OK for latency but throughput drops weirdly under batching. sharing heatmap in a sec :eyes:
Jordan: thanks. what's baseline we care about?
Maya: target: 22B throughput >= 160 tokens/s @ batch=8, p50 gen latency < 180ms/token on A100-80GB. Baseline (Orion14B) was ~200 tokens/s at batch=8.
Kevin: got a repro script? can run on dedicated infra.
Maya: yes. small harness we used: 
```bash
python bench.py --model=lucid22b --device=gpu --batch=8 --seq=1024 --quant=int8 --trials=50
```
Sasha: quick note — int4 quant gave a 20% quality regression vs float16 on our eval set. int8 looks closer.
Maya: correct. int8 perf looked promising but throughput drops when seq>1024. suspect KV cache flush overhead + kernel fallback path.
BenchBot: scheduled job 4187654321-heatmap-run on pool-gpu-2. ETA 12m.
Linh: can you post perf logs? curious about SSE warnings / launch fallbacks.
Maya: pasting trimmed logs: 
```
[2026-03-19 12:04:03] launch_kernel: chosen=fast_attn_v2, fallback=slow_attn_v1, path_cost_delta=+0.37
[2026-03-19 12:04:03] kv_cache_miss: sequence_window=2048, triggers=3
[2026-03-19 12:04:08] batch_coalesce: padding_overhead=18%
```
Priya: padding overhead 18% is significant. what's sequence distribution used?
Maya: mixed; we used sampled client traces: mean seq=1200, 25th=64, 75th=1800. That explains padding.
Jordan: two quick experiments: 1) ctx-aware batching (group by seq_len buckets), 2) prefix-KV warmup for long tails.
Kevin: agree. also check conv kernel choice for kv layout; older kernels prefer 128-aligned dims. misalignment triggers slow path.
Sasha: run idea: compare batch=4/8/16 with ctx_bucketed batching and record tokens/s and p95 latency. Make heatmap over (batch, seq).
Maya: doing that now. config used: 
```json
{"model":"lucid22b","quant":"int8","kernels":"auto","batch_buckets":[64,256,1024,2048],"warmup_prefix":128}
```
BenchBot: run complete. uploading heatmap -> https://internal.redwood/bench/4187654321/heatmap.png :upload: (3.2MB)
Priya: looks like tokens/s drops steeply for seq>=1500 at batch>=8. bucketed batching recovers ~30% of throughput for long seqs.
Linh: any asymmetric perf across cards? NVLink/PCIe topology?
Maya: yes — node2 has PCIe-only cards, node3 NVLink. node3 ~1.6x throughput for long seqs.
Jordan: action items: 
- Maya/Kevin: run kernel alignment probe (pad dims to 128, 256) and re-run heatmap (due EOD)
- Sasha: evaluate quality delta int8 vs f16 on eval shard A (50 prompts)
- Priya: check routing policy to prefer NVLink nodes for seq>1024 until we have better kernel path
- Linh: add KV warmup flow to bench harness so cache hit-rate improves after first token window
Maya: I'll attach run artifacts and a quick checklist: 
1) reproduce on dedicated NVLink node
2) kernel padding sweep: pad heads to 128/256, record kernel selection
3) batch bucket config tuning and beam/greedy latency check
4) quant quality eval (Sasha)
5) deploy-rollout gating rule: restrict int8 to pilot traffic if p95 latency < 500ms and quality delta < 3%
Kevin: I'll take kernel padding sweep. tagging @DeployBot for temporary routing rule.
DeployBot: routing rule applied: prefer node3 for requests with seq_len>1024 for traffic=pilot, expires=6h.
Sasha: started eval run, will post summary in ~45m. early headcount: int8 RLHF examples look okay but longer instruction responses trim slightly.
Maya: thanks. will follow up with consolidated heatmap and a short PR with bench config changes. :thumbsup:
Jordan: nice. keep it short — we should have a final go/no-go doc for int8 pilot tomorrow morning.
Maya: noted. closing loop after kernel sweep.
